title: Choose BuildChamp's visual world
question: Which world makes a six-pick run feel quick, social, and worth sharing?

options.label: Arcade Versus Ticket
options.lineage: arcade tournament tickets, thermal score slips, and cabinet challenge cards
options.thesis: Every champion reveal prints a claim ticket; locking a part tears it into a six-slot challenger strip.
options.viewport: A large current-champion reveal sits above a tactile six-ticket build rail, with one unmistakable lock action and no lobby friction.
options.risk: Arcade references can become noisy unless the champion and remaining slots always dominate.

options.label: Queue Board
options.lineage: rail concourse split-flap boards at rush hour
options.thesis: Six fixed rows become a live departure board where each champion cascades into view and a claimed part becomes permanent.
options.case: Excellent state clarity, but the travel metaphor identifies less strongly with the Discord party-game audience.
options.viewport: The active reveal occupies the top row while six ruled part rows show open, available, and locked states at a glance.
options.risk: The rigid timetable can make a playful run feel procedural if animation and copy lack warmth.

options.label: Deployable Champion
options.lineage: Miura-fold aerospace sheets unfolding from a compact packet
options.thesis: Each irreversible choice locks one linked crease until the completed champion deploys as a single shareable sheet.
options.case: The whole-from-six mechanism is exceptionally truthful, but its unfamiliar controls need more teaching.
options.viewport: A partially unfolded champion field fills the screen, with the current reveal anchored to the next unlocked crease cell.
options.risk: The geometric metaphor may slow a game meant to launch casually between matches.

options.label: Party Console
options.lineage: pill-cornered starship wall panels and color-banked control consoles
options.thesis: Six bold console banks surround the active champion; one press reroutes that champion's part into the permanent build.
options.case: Playful and fast with strong controls, though the sci-fi language is less specifically League-social than the ticket world.
options.viewport: A sweeping elbow frame contains the reveal while six large color banks expose every available pick without scrolling.
options.risk: The console may read as decorative fiction if labels and hierarchy do not remain brutally clear.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark gaming interface with a champion splash, six ability cards, and a conventional results panel.
canonCard.viewport: A centered champion card sits above a familiar six-card selection grid and primary lock button.
canonCard.risk: Immediately legible, but easy to mistake for any unofficial League companion tool.
